mcqs.question: Which statement best compares epithelial tissue with connective tissue regarding cell arrangement and extracellular matrix?

options.A: Epithelial tissue has loosely arranged cells with abundant extracellular matrix, whereas connective tissue has tightly packed cells with little matrix.
options.B: Epithelial tissue consists of tightly packed cells with minimal extracellular matrix, while connective tissue has scattered cells embedded in abundant extracellular matrix.
options.C: Both epithelial and connective tissues have similar cell density and extracellular matrix composition.
options.D: Epithelial tissue lacks a basement membrane, unlike connective tissue which always has one.

mcqs.answer: Epithelial tissue consists of tightly packed cells with minimal extracellular matrix, while connective tissue has scattered cells embedded in abundant extracellular matrix.
mcqs.explanation: Epithelial tissue is characterized by cells that are closely packed together with very little extracellular material, forming continuous sheets that cover surfaces. In contrast, connective tissue has relatively few cells that are separated by a large amount of extracellular matrix, which provides support and flexibility. Option B correctly captures this distinction, while the other options contain inaccurate statements.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify major types of epithelial tissue
mcqs.question: Which of the following lists includes all the major categories of epithelial tissue as described in NCERT Class 9?

options.A: Simple squamous, stratified cuboidal, pseudostratified columnar, transitional.
options.B: Simple squamous, simple cuboidal, simple columnar, stratified squamous, pseudostratified columnar, transitional.
options.C: Simple cuboidal, stratified squamous, glandular, muscular.
options.D: Simple columnar, stratified columnar, pseudostratified squamous, keratinized.

mcqs.answer: Simple squamous, simple cuboidal, simple columnar, stratified squamous, pseudostratified columnar, transitional.
mcqs.explanation: NCERT Chapter on Tissues lists six major types of epithelial tissue: simple squamous, simple cuboidal, simple columnar, stratified squamous, pseudostratified columnar, and transitional. Option B contains exactly these six types. The other options either omit some types or include unrelated categories such as muscular tissue.

mcqs.question: How does the thin, flat structure of simple squamous epithelium relate to its function?

options.A: Provides a thick barrier to protect underlying tissues.
options.B: Facilitates rapid diffusion and filtration across membranes.
options.C: Allows for secretion of large amounts of mucus.

mcqs.answer: Facilitates rapid diffusion and filtration across membranes.
mcqs.explanation: Simple squamous epithelium is composed of a single layer of flat cells, minimizing the distance over which substances must travel. This structural feature makes it ideal for diffusion and filtration, such as in alveoli and glomeruli. Options A, C, and D describe functions of other epithelial types or tissues.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches an epithelial type with its primary role in the body?

options.A: Stratified squamous epithelium – absorption of nutrients.
options.B: Simple columnar epithelium – protection against abrasion.
options.C: Simple cuboidal epithelium – secretion of hormones.
options.D: Stratified squamous epithelium – protection; simple columnar epithelium – absorption.

mcqs.answer: Stratified squamous epithelium – protection; simple columnar epithelium – absorption.
mcqs.explanation: Stratified squamous epithelium, found on skin and oral cavity, protects against mechanical injury. Simple columnar epithelium, lining the intestine, has microvilli that increase surface area for absorption. The other options incorrectly assign roles.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines epithelial tissue?

options.A: A tissue composed of loosely arranged cells with abundant extracellular matrix.
options.B: A tissue that lines body surfaces and cavities, consisting of tightly packed cells with little extracellular matrix.
options.C: A tissue that primarily stores fat and provides insulation.
options.D: A tissue that forms the bulk of the skeletal system.

mcqs.answer: A tissue that lines body surfaces and cavities, consisting of tightly packed cells with little extracellular matrix.
mcqs.explanation: Epithelial tissue forms continuous sheets that cover external and internal surfaces. Its cells are closely packed with minimal extracellular material, allowing it to act as a barrier and interface. Options A, C, and D describe connective, adipose, and skeletal tissues respectively.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify major types of epithelial tissue
mcqs.question: The thin lining that allows gas exchange in the alveoli of the lungs is an example of which type of epithelium?
mcqs.explanation: Alveolar walls are composed of simple squamous epithelium because its single, flat cell layer permits efficient diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide. The other listed types are too thick or have different functions.

mcqs.question: The lining of the small intestine, which has numerous microvilli to increase surface area, exemplifies which relationship between structure and function?

options.A: Thick multilayered cells for protection, unrelated to absorption.
options.B: Simple squamous cells facilitating diffusion of gases.
options.C: Simple columnar epithelium with apical microvilli enhancing absorption.
options.D: Stratified cuboidal epithelium providing secretion of enzymes.

mcqs.answer: Simple columnar epithelium with apical microvilli enhancing absorption.
mcqs.explanation: The small intestine is lined by simple columnar epithelium. The presence of microvilli on the apical surface dramatically increases the absorptive surface area, matching the function of nutrient absorption. Options A, B, and D describe mismatched structures and functions.

mcqs.question: A person suffers a cut on the skin. The rapid formation of a new protective layer over the wound is primarily due to which role of epithelial tissue?

options.A: Absorptive role of simple columnar epithelium.
options.B: Protective role of stratified squamous epithelium.
options.D: Transport role of simple cuboidal epithelium.

mcqs.answer: Protective role of stratified squamous epithelium.
mcqs.explanation: Skin is composed of stratified squamous epithelium, which provides a durable barrier against mechanical injury and pathogens. After a cut, keratinocyte proliferation restores this protective layer. The other options refer to unrelated functions or tissue types.
